The graph of $y=f(x),$ shown above, consists of two line segments. Find the value of ${\int }_{-4}^{6}f(x)\,\text{d}x.$
feedback.worked_solution:
We divide the interval of integration into $3$ regions: the line segment for $x\in [-4,0],$ the line segment for $x\in (0,4],$ and the line segment for $x\in [4,6].$ Therefore, we can write the required integral as follows:

$$
{\int }_{-4}^{6}f(x)\,\text{d}x={{{\int }_{-4}^{0}f(x)\,\text{d}x}_{⏟}}_{{A}_{1}}+{{{\int }_{0}^{4}f(x)\,\text{d}x}_{⏟}}_{{A}_{2}}+{{{\int }_{4}^{6}f(x)\,\text{d}x}_{⏟}}_{-{A}_{3}}
$$

- The $1$st integral represents the signed area between the curve and the $x$-axis, where $x\in [-4,0].$ The corresponding region is a trapezoid, so we find the area using the formula

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}_{1} & =\frac{1}{2}(a+b)h \\  & =\frac{1}{2}(1+3)(4) \\  & =8.\end{aligned}
$$

- The $2$nd integral represents the signed area between the curve and the $x$-axis, where $x\in (0,4].$ The corresponding region is a right triangle, so we find the area using the formula

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}_{2} & =\frac{1}{2}bh \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\cdot 4\cdot 2 \\  & =4.\end{aligned}
$$

- The $3$rd integral represents the signed area between the curve and the $x$-axis, where $x\in [4,6].$ The corresponding region is a right triangle, so we find the area using the formula

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}_{3} & =\frac{1}{2}bh \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\cdot 2\cdot 1 \\  & =1.\end{aligned}
$$

Since the region lies below the $x$-axis, we have

$$
{\int }_{4}^{6}f(x)\,\text{d}x=-{A}_{3}=-1.
$$

Finally, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{-4}^{6}f(x)\,\text{d}x & ={A}_{1}+{A}_{2}-{A}_{3} \\  & =8+4-1 \\  & =11.\end{aligned}
$$
